rules.rule: Check for urgent and likely gum/teeth conditions
rules.problem: Trigger (Tooth finding OR Gingivae finding) matches 'gum/teeth symptoms'; the check_for list covers every red-box item and every discriminating finding of the three 'likely' boxes. 'May have tooth pain with hot or cold food/drink' is omitted, which is defensible since it is not discriminating. Swelling-next-to-tooth concept could be 'Dental swelling'.

'Dental caries likely' → probable is correct; the OR of staining/holes-pits/missing teeth follows the page's 'or' list. Concepts are a little broad: staining loses brown/black at gumline, and missing teeth alone triggers caries.

The page text 'Previous/current tooth pain with pus in mouth, swelling next to tooth' is ambiguous: the comma could mean 'and' or 'or'. The rule ANDs all three, so a patient with tooth pain and pus but no visible swelling (or swelling without visible pus) gets no abscess diagnosis. Plausible readings are (and toothache (or pus swelling)) or all three. AND is the strictest choice and needs recording as a judgement call. Also, 'Previous' pain isn't represented.

rules.rule: Urgent: gum/teeth symptoms with danger signs
rules.problem: Urgent is justified by 'Give urgent attention… Refer urgently'. Structure (and complaint (or (and T>=38 (or swelling face/jaw/next to tooth)) unable to eat, unable to drink, spontaneous toothache, night toothache)) matches the red box exactly, including that fever must co-occur with swelling. The 'wakes at night' and 'next to tooth' concepts are slightly imprecise.

summary: The rules are faithful overall: the red box maps exactly onto an Urgent rule, including the temperature-AND-swelling conjunction, and all three 'likely' boxes become probable diagnoses. The most consequential issue is that the dental abscess rule ANDs toothache, pus and swelling next to tooth, while the page's comma list could equally mean pus OR swelling. AND is the strictest reading and may miss abscesses. Smaller points: 'Dental swelling' (finding) is a closer concept for 'swelling next to tooth'; 'Night time' doesn't encode 'wakes patient'; staining loses brown/black at gumline; and 'Tooth absent' alone yields probable caries.
